title: F-18 SBAR Upgrade BOA Addition
description: This notice serves as a pre-solicitation notice for the addition of NSN 4810 017423274, Part Number 2770073-115, Nomenclature: Fluid Pressure Regulating Valve (SBAR) to the five-year strategic sustainment solution (S-3) Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N00383-24-G-BN01 with Parker Hannifin Corp (Cage 59211). The addition will support future overhaul and upgrades of the current -114 SBAR configuration in support of a logistic engineering change proposal (LECP). The addition of the -115 SBAR will be for a quantity 836 upgrades and are planned between FY�27 through FY�29. See accompanying Draft RFP for additional details. Based on the above, the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source (Parker Hannifin, Cage 59211) under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. The Government does not possess (or cannot provide) the data necessary to perform the required overhaul and upgrade of the item. The applicable PSC is 4810, The applicable NAICS is 336413. The item under this acquisition is subject to the Free Trade Agreements Act and/or the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. All responsible sources may identify their interest and provide capability statements in response to this notice. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responses received within 15 days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Source Approval is required prior to award. An alternate source must qualify in accordance with the design control activity�s procedures, as approved by the cognizant Government engineering activity WSS will not delay award while Source Approval is pending. If you are not an approved source you must submit, together with your proposal, the information detailed in the NAVSUP WSS Source Approval Information Brochure for Repair and/or Spares. This brochure identifies technical data required to be submitted based on your company's experience in repair of the same or similar items. This brochure can be obtained at: https://www.navsup.navy.mil/NAVSUP-Enterprise/NAVSUP-Weapon-Systems-Support/Business-Opps/ If your request for source approval is currently being evaluated at NAVSUP WSS, submit with your response a copy of the cover letter that forwarded your request for source approval. Responses received which fail to provide all data required by the Source Approval Brochure or document previous submission of all data required by the Source Approval Brochure will not be considered. Please note, if evaluation of a source approval request submitted hereunder cannot be processed in time and/or approval requirements preclude the ability to obtain subject items in time to meet Government requirements, award of the subject requirement will continue based on Fleet support needs. For any questions concerning this notice, contact the PCO, Christopher Letts at Christopher.j.letts2.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Katsomo- ja katoshanke 9/2026
description: Katsomo- ja katoshanke 9/2026 1. HANKINNAN KOHDE JA TAVOITTEET Kuusan nuorisoseura ry pyytää tarjouksia katsomo- ja katoshankkeesta. Hanke käsittää seuraavat kokonaisuudet: (Tarkemmin leikkaus A-A suunnitelmissa) -Kesäteatterin katsomo: n. 500 paikkaa ja Katsomon katos: n. 330 m² (suunnitelmien mukaan) -Maatyöt, tukimuuri, salaoja- ja sadevesijärjestelmä, routasuojaus + alaosan antura Tilaaja toteuttaa osan töistä talkoilla. 2. URAKAN SISÄLTÖ JA TARJOUSPYYNTÖ Hanke sisältää kaksi (2) eri tarjottavaa kokonaisurakkaa (tarjouksen tulee sisältää kaikki työt, tarvikkeet, matkakulut ja velvoitteet): – 1 Katsomo (n. 500 paikkaa), katsomon katos (n. 330 m²) sekä kaikki näihin liittyvät rakennustekniset työt ja perustukset, rakenne- ja erikoissuunnitelmat, sekä rakennusvalvonnan vaatiman päärakennesuunnittelijan - 2 Maanrakennustyöt, maanpaineseinä rakennesuunnitelmineen sekä routasuojaus. - Tarjoajan tulee antaa kiinteähintainen tarjous kustakin tarjoamastaan kohdasta (1-2) erikseen (alv 0 %). - Hankkeen lupakuvat ja rajapinnat löytyvät tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevista suunnitelmista ja dokumenteista. Tarjousten pohjana käytetään lupakuvia. - Tarjousten voimassaoloaika 3 kk. - Tilaaja ei käsittele vaihtoehtotarjouksia. - Melua aiheuttavat työt pitää suorittaa arkipäivinä klo 7.00-18.00 välisenä aikana (muina aikoina tarvitaan tilaajalta etukäteistä hyväksyntää). - aikataulutus sovitaan urakoitsijoiden kesken päätösvaiheessa. - Molempien osa-alueiden urakoitsija toimii pääurakoitsijana ja lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana oman osuuden kohdalla. AIKATAULU, VIIVÄSTYSSAKKO JA TAKUU Aikataulu on kriittinen kesäteatterin esityskauden vuoksi. -Purku: Tilaaja purkaa vanhat rakenteet (poislukien perustukset) talkoilla vuoden 2026 aikana. -Työmaan aloitus: 15.3.2027 (sään salliessa). -Hanke maanrakennuksen ja maanpaineseinän osalta valmis: 15.4.2027 (kohde vastaanotettuna ja siivottuna). -Hanke katsomon ja katoksen osalta osalta valmis: 15.6.2027 (kohde vastaanotettuna ja siivottuna). -Erityishuomio: 3.5.2027 alkaen näyttämöalueen on oltava vapaana teatterin käyttöön ilta-aikoina ja viikonloppuisin sekä sinne pitää pystyä rakentamaan näytelmän kulissit. -Työmaatuvallisuus: Nuorisoseuran piha ja talo on käytössä hankkeen ajan, joka pitää ottaa huomioon. Hankkeen on tarkoitus valmistua 15.6.2027 mennessä Viivästyssakko: - Mikäli kohde ei ole vastaanottokelpoinen 15.6.2027 mennessä, urakoitsija maksaa viivästyssakkoa 1,0 % (alv 0 %) urakkahinnasta per alkava viikko. - Mikäli viivästys jatkuu 1.7.2027 yli, tilaajalla on oikeus periä sakon lisäksi korvaus välittömistä taloudellisista vahingoista (esim. menetetyt tulot kesäteatterikaudelta). Takuu: -Yleinen takuuaika: 2 vuotta (alkaa koko urakan hyväksytystä vastaanotosta). -Erityistakuu: vesikate 10 vuotta ja teräsrakenteet 5 vuotta. -Kymmenvuotisvastuu: YSE 1998 mukainen vastuu piilevistä virheistä 10 vuotta. -Urakoitsijan on asetettava rakennusalan yleisten sopimusehtojen (YSE 1998) mukaiset vakuudet. *Rakennusajan vakuus on 10 % urakkahinnasta (alv 0 %) *Takuuajan vakuus 2 % urakkahinnasta (alv 0 %). Vakuuden on oltava voimassa 3 kk yli takuuajan päättymisen. *Vakuudeksi hyväksytään pankkitakaus, vakuutusyhtiön takaus tai tilaajan hyväksymä muu vakuus.ALIURAKOITSIJAT -Urakoitsija on velvollinen ilmoittamaan käyttämänsä aliurakoitsijat tilaajalle ennen näiden työn aloitusta. Tilaajavastuulain mukaiset todistukset vaaditaan koko ketjulta. -Tilaajalla on oikeus hylätä aliurakoitsija, mikäli tämä ei täytä asetettuja soveltuvuusvaatimuksia tai tilaajavastuulain mukaisia velvoitteita. Muuta: -Voimassa olevat tulityö- ja työturvallisuuskortit sekä veronumero kaikilla työntekijöillä. -Nuorisoseuran pihan ja talon aktiivinen käyttö on huomioitava työturvallisuudessa. TARJOAJIEN POISSULKEMINEN JA SOVELTUVUUS SEKÄ ESITTELYT(Hankintalaki 1397/2016) Pakolliset poissulkemisperusteet (80 §): Hankintayksikkö sulkee tarjoajan pois kilpailutuksesta, mikäli tarjoajaa tai sen hallinto-, johto- tai valvontaelimen jäsentä koskee hankintalain 80 §:ssä tarkoitettu lainvoimainen tuomio. Harkinnanvaraiset poissulkemisperusteet (81 §): Hankintayksikkö voi sulkea tarjoajan pois kilpailutuksesta, jos tarjoaja: -On konkurssissa, purkamis- tai saneerausmenettelyssä. -On syyllistynyt ammattitoiminnassaan vakavaan virheeseen. -On laiminlyönyt verojen tai sosiaaliturvamaksujen maksamisen. -On aiemmissa hankintasopimuksissa syyllistynyt merkittäviin puutteisiin. Tarjoajan on täytettävä tilaajavastuulain (1233/2006) mukaiset velvoitteet. Soveltuvuuden arvioimiseksi tarjoajan tulee toimittaa: -Enintään 3 kk vanhat todistukset verojen maksamisesta, eläkevakuutuksista ja työehtosopimuksesta. -Selvitys voimassa olevasta vastuuvakuutuksesta (vähintään 500 000 €) . - Kohteeseen tutustuminen on suositeltavaa. -Tarjouksen ja liitteiden tulee olla suomenkielisiä. - Yhteyshenkilö: Tapio Myllylä, 043 824 8504, tapio@rakennussuunnittelumyllyla.fi.Sijainti: Koskelantie 43, 41370 Kuusa.,

title: Domestic Guard Services
description: ALL INTERESTED OFFERORS SHALL NEED TO a) REQUEST EXPLICIT ACCESS VIA FBO FOR D OCUMENTS POSTED b) THROUGHLY REVIEW PARAGRAPH 4, 5 AND 6 GIVEN HEREIN 1. The U.S. Department of State (DoS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide highly trained and professional security force, hereinafter referred to as the DoS Diplomatic Security, Uniformed Protective Division (UPD), which directly support the Domestic Facilities Protection Office (DS/DO/DFP). This requirement is to manage protection security force to: a) Protect life and property, b) Protect and control classified/sensitive information/property, c) Prevent unauthorized access to facilities or other venues und er charge of DS; d) Maintain order at DoS facilities or other venues under charge of DS. e) Deter criminal activity and when appropriate, apprehend violators in and around all DoS controlled facilities or other venues under charge of DS nation-wide, to include Hawaii, Alaska, and Puerto Rico. 2. The Contractor shall be expected to provide their organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the solicitation Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). 3. Required NAICS is 561612 4. Recommended or suggested requirements for this effort are as follows: a) The Offeror should have at least 10 years' overall experience providing 24/7 Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services to the United States Government or the private sector (must be able to provide evidence of at least 3 Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services contracts performed during the last 10 years) as part of their experience and past performance. b) The Offeror should be able to demonstrate that at least one (1) of the contracts referred to in paragraph a) above was valued at a minimum of $400 million. c) The Offeror should have employed at least 500 Armed Uniformed Protective guards, inclusive of at least five (5) Explosive Detection Dog Teams, in performance of at least one (1) of its Uniformed Protective Guard Services contracts within the last five (5) years. Meaning, the contract should have included both uniformed armed protective services and EDD teams (teams could have been subcontracted). d) The Offeror should have performed Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services domestically (within the continental United States) in at least 50 differently situated locations, with at least 15 sites physically located domestically in multiple States, (inclusive of Hawaii, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico) within the last ten (10) years. e) In addition to the above, the Offeror should have performance experience within the last 5 years, providing Armed Mobile Patrol Uniformed Protective Guards. f) The contractor should have experience within the last 3 years providing Armed Uniformed Protective Guards cleared in protecting classified up to Top Secret. g) The Offer or should have past/current experience in Collective Bargaining Agreements/Contract Negotiations. h) The Offeror should have past/current performance experience within the last 3 years operating a Uniformed Protective Guards (UPO's) Centralized Command Center, wherein uniformed protective guards are utilized in dispatching UPO's to calls for service as well monitoring alarms (fire and Intrusion Detection Systems) and making notifications (email and phone) to senior management. i) The Offeror should have experience within the last 3 years providing Armed Uniformed Protective Guards that have handled demonstrations numbering at least 100 demonstrators. 5. All contracted personnel, regardless of nationality, will be required to pass a background investigation conducted by the Contractor and a separate background investigation conducted by the U.S. Government to certify their suitability for employment under this contract. The expected security complement is anticipated to be approximately no less than 1,270 (excluding Corporate and indirect support). 6. Contractors shall be required to have a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) for this contract with Security, Police, and Fire Professionals of America (SPFPA) and Locals 644, 645, 646, and 647, plus any other union determined to be necessary or needed for the successful completion of this contract. 7. The approximate acquisition schedule is as follows: a) Offerors will have approximately six weeks to prepare proposals as given in the posted instructions. All dates are subject to change and any change will be posted on this site via amendments. b) No pre-proposal site visit will be scheduled. c) Questions regarding the content of this solicitation shall be due by 09/04/2026 as instructed in Section L. There will only be one (1) round of questions. Responses to questions will only be provided to those questions deemed relevant and substantive. 8. Offerors shall have an active registration on the System for Award Management at https://www.SAM.gov. It shall be the Contractor's responsibility to ensure vendor's information is accurate on SAM.gov. . 9. Offerors shall be required to request access documents via sam.gov. Only two (2) representatives from each firm will be allowed Explicit Access in an effort to control access to sensitive but unclassified documents. Access will be granted AFTER the documents are posted and when the Government POC receives a sam.gov electronic explicit access request email notice. Contractor is responsible for all aspects of obtaining access. PHONE CALLS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

title: Sources Sought for OR FS FREWN602 28(1), Forest Road 28 Reconstruction
description: Sources Sought for OR FS FREWN602 28(1), Forest Road 28 Reconstruction This solicitation is a "REQUEST FOR INFORMATION" only for the proposed contract work listed in the requirements section below. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing �one-time use� items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management � Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. The intent of this requirement is to provide one (1) new Red Dragon �Dragon Eggs� Delayed Chemical Ignition Dispenser to be used during prescribed burning and wildfire incidents. The Red Dragon Dispensers are the only aerial ignition devices in USDA-FS inventory and the only aerial ignition device authorized for use by the Wildland Fire Aerial Ignition Operations as directed by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) PMS 501, Chapter 3. By awarding a Purchase Order for the supply of SEI Industries, Red Dragon Delayed Chemical Ignition Dispensers through Helifire LLC, the USDA/Forest Service ensures equipment performance, OEM equipment support, operational reliability, system continuity, operator and equipment safety, and existing factory warranties, while ensuring maximum mission readiness, meeting the strategic objectives of the Wildland Fire Aerial Ignition Operations of our organization. The PPS, IPO, AIMS intends to non-competitively award this requirement to Helifire LLC. The required items are proprietary to SEI Industries, LLC and the only authorized vendor to provide SEI Industries, Red Dragon dispensers, is Helifire LLC. Furthermore, Red Dragons are compatible in all aspects with existing SEI Industries systems/equipment presently in use, allowing personnel in the field to maintain continuity of service during fire mission times. No other manufacturer is compatible or can interchange with SEI Industries� proprietary systems without voiding existing warranties and posing safety risks to equipment and operators. As a result, any vendor other than Helifire LLC capable of providing comparable models would not be approved by the manufacturer or per established USDA-FS equipment approvals. Helifire LLC is the only source capable of providing the authorized required items to maintain the safety of personnel, equipment, continuity of service, and the uninterrupted operation and mission readiness during fire seasons. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 115310 with the size standard of $34.0 million. This notice of intent is not a request for proposals or quotes. description: SYNOPSIS The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), C3BM?Directorate,?Wright Patterson?Force Base (WPAFB),?Ohio?is conducting market research seeking vendor interest for?a?Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System. ? PURPOSE The Government is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing solutions for a Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System that fires affordable munitions, enables defense against air and missile threats with an initial focus on subsonic cruise missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to provide persistent defense in support of United States Air Force assets. The objective of this RFI is to gather information regarding industry capability. ACQUISITION STRATEGY? The program's acquisition strategy is currently in development.? SCOPE/REQUIREMENTS The scope of this RFI is centered on solutions that strictly prioritize fifteen baseline attributes essential to operational success that can engage both cruise missiles and UAS (groups 1-5) threats in accordance with the reference documents. To effectively assess and compare air defense weapon system performance, there are fifteen critical baseline operational and technical parameters that must be analyzed in unison. These key metrics begin with the system's Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) evaluated against both Cruise Missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5 at maximum range and altitude, ensuring robust lethality against diverse modern threats. The physical footprint of the engagement envelope is defined by its Effective Slant Range and Elevation Coverage, while the capacity for sustained operations is dictated by Magazine Depth and the system's ability to execute Raid Handling against saturating attacks. Furthermore, modern multi-domain operations require seamless Integrated Sensor Capability, deep C2 System Integration, and broad System Interoperability across joint networks. From an efficiency and sustainment standpoint, the system must balance its Cost Per Engagement and Manpower requirements, supported by a reliable Built-in-Test (BIT) framework for rapid diagnostics. Finally, tactical utility is rounded out by the platform's overall Transportability, stringent Weapon Safety protocols, and its comprehensive Multi-Domain Engagement Capability to counter threats across various operational environments. Fifteen Baseline Requirements: Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs CM at max range and altitude Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs UAS Groups 1-5 at max range and altitude Effective Slant Range Elevation Coverage Magazine Depth Raid Handling Integrated Sensor Capability C2 System Integration System Interoperability Cost Per Engagement Manpower Built-in-Test (BIT) Transportability Weapon Safety Multi-Domain Engagement Capability When designing and evaluating next-generation defense systems, the development team must navigate critical trade-offs across three primary Trade Space Attributes to balance lethality, situational awareness, and operational flexibility. First, the system must optimize Munition Performance versus Munition Cost and Gun Capability, ensuring that the interceptor's velocity, maneuverability, and terminal effects are maximized without driving the cost-per-engagement to unsustainable levels or exceeding the physical constraints of the host platform. Second, developers must carefully select the Organic Sensor Capability and Phenomenology�integrating the right mix of radar, electro-optical, infrared, or radio-frequency sensors�to ensure reliable target acquisition and tracking across varying weather conditions, environments, and countermeasure scenarios. Finally, the entire architecture must remain Rapidly Deployable, maintaining a lightweight, modular, and transportable footprint that can be swiftly projected into austere theater environments to meet emergent threats. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the F/A-18 and EA-18G Program Office (PMA-265), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a market research tool to identify potential parties having an interest, knowledge and resources required to support manufacturing, assembly and installation of Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) 6315C3 A-Kits Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) ECP 6315C3. The NAVWAR A-Kits support aircraft integration for both United States Navy (USN) and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) F/A-18 and EA-18G configurations. This effort encompasses engineering and manufacturing tasks include, but are not limited to: Manufacturing assembly planning and execution. Structural sheet metal fabrication, machining, and finishing. Electrical wiring harness and RF cabling assembly. Evaluation of engineering design drawings to determine component and manufacturing requirements. Procurement of all associated parts, specialty tooling, and raw materials. Program reporting and quality control documentation. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining from The Boeing Company all aircraft data, manufacturing specifications, and proprietary specification data necessary to manufacture and install the A-Kits. The Boeing Company is the only known source that possesses requisite technical data, unique and specialized engineering capability, subject matter expertise, resources, tooling, facilities, and manufacturing processes used on the F/A-18 and EA-18G aircraft platforms. title: Domestic Guard Services
description: ALL INTERESTED OFFERORS SHALL NEED TO a) REQUEST EXPLICIT ACCESS VIA FBO FOR D OCUMENTS POSTED b) THROUGHLY REVIEW PARAGRAPH 4, 5 AND 6 GIVEN HEREIN 1. The U.S. Department of State (DoS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide highly trained and professional security force, hereinafter referred to as the DoS Diplomatic Security, Uniformed Protective Division (UPD), which directly support the Domestic Facilities Protection Office (DS/DO/DFP). This requirement is to manage protection security force to: a) Protect life and property, b) Protect and control classified/sensitive information/property, c) Prevent unauthorized access to facilities or other venues und er charge of DS; d) Maintain order at DoS facilities or other venues under charge of DS. e) Deter criminal activity and when appropriate, apprehend violators in and around all DoS controlled facilities or other venues under charge of DS nation-wide, to include Hawaii, Alaska, and Puerto Rico. 2. The Contractor shall be expected to provide their organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the solicitation Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). 3. Required NAICS is 561612 4. Recommended or suggested requirements for this effort are as follows: a) The Offeror should have at least 10 years' overall experience providing 24/7 Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services to the United States Government or the private sector (must be able to provide evidence of at least 3 Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services contracts performed during the last 10 years) as part of their experience and past performance. b) The Offeror should be able to demonstrate that at least one (1) of the contracts referred to in paragraph a) above was valued at a minimum of $400 million. c) The Offeror should have employed at least 500 Armed Uniformed Protective guards, inclusive of at least five (5) Explosive Detection Dog Teams, in performance of at least one (1) of its Uniformed Protective Guard Services contracts within the last five (5) years. Meaning, the contract should have included both uniformed armed protective services and EDD teams (teams could have been subcontracted). d) The Offeror should have performed Armed Uniformed Protective Guard Services domestically (within the continental United States) in at least 50 differently situated locations, with at least 15 sites physically located domestically in multiple States, (inclusive of Hawaii, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico) within the last ten (10) years. e) In addition to the above, the Offeror should have performance experience within the last 5 years, providing Armed Mobile Patrol Uniformed Protective Guards. f) The contractor should have experience within the last 3 years providing Armed Uniformed Protective Guards cleared in protecting classified up to Top Secret. g) The Offer or should have past/current experience in Collective Bargaining Agreements/Contract Negotiations. h) The Offeror should have past/current performance experience within the last 3 years operating a Uniformed Protective Guards (UPO's) Centralized Command Center, wherein uniformed protective guards are utilized in dispatching UPO's to calls for service as well monitoring alarms (fire and Intrusion Detection Systems) and making notifications (email and phone) to senior management. i) The Offeror should have experience within the last 3 years providing Armed Uniformed Protective Guards that have handled demonstrations numbering at least 100 demonstrators. 5. All contracted personnel, regardless of nationality, will be required to pass a background investigation conducted by the Contractor and a separate background investigation conducted by the U.S. Government to certify their suitability for employment under this contract. The expected security complement is anticipated to be approximately no less than 1,270 (excluding Corporate and indirect support). 6. Contractors shall be required to have a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) for this contract with Security, Police, and Fire Professionals of America (SPFPA) and Locals 644, 645, 646, and 647, plus any other union determined to be necessary or needed for the successful completion of this contract. 7. The approximate acquisition schedule is as follows: a) Offerors will have approximately six weeks to prepare proposals as given in the posted instructions. All dates are subject to change and any change will be posted on this site via amendments. b) No pre-proposal site visit will be scheduled. c) Questions regarding the content of this solicitation shall be due by 09/04/2026 as instructed in Section L. There will only be one (1) round of questions. Responses to questions will only be provided to those questions deemed relevant and substantive. 8. Offerors shall have an active registration on the System for Award Management at https://www.SAM.gov. It shall be the Contractor's responsibility to ensure vendor's information is accurate on SAM.gov. . 9. Offerors shall be required to request access documents via sam.gov. Only two (2) representatives from each firm will be allowed Explicit Access in an effort to control access to sensitive but unclassified documents. Access will be granted AFTER the documents are posted and when the Government POC receives a sam.gov electronic explicit access request email notice. Contractor is responsible for all aspects of obtaining access. PHONE CALLS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

Området indrettes med fokus på trafiksikkerhed og funktionalitet, herunder tydelig adskillelse af kørende og gående trafik samt sikre gangforbindelser mellem parkeringsarealerne, bygningerne og områdets øvrige funktioner. title: Udbud af rammeaftale vedrørende levering af pædagogiske vikarer til Hillerød Kommune
description: Udbuddet omfatter levering af pædagogiske vikarer til daginstitutioner i Hillerød Kommune. Ydelserne omfatter alene vikartimer afholdt i dagtimer på hverdage inden for følgende kategorier af vikarer:PædagogerPædagogmedhjælperePædagogiske assistenterAftalen er rettet mod Ordregivers daginstitutioner, der har et behov for vikarer. Ordregiver kan og vil indgå aftaler om levering af pædagogiske vikarer rettet mod andre typer af behov og afdelinger, som fx vikarer til botilbud og andre særtilbud.Aftalen omfatter er rettet mod levering af vikarer, når Ordregivers eget vikarkorps samt Ordregivers faste pædagoger, pædagogmedhjælpere mv. ikke kan dække behovet. Krav til vikarerne samt vilkår for bestilling og levering fremgår af Aftalen med tilhørende bilag - herunder særligt Bilag 1 – Kravspecifikation.Der arbejdes med to overordnede typer af vikarbestillinger: Akutvikarer og Planlagte Vikarer.Aftalen giver ikke vindende tilbudsgiver krav på eller garanti for et bestemt antal timer/vagter. Leverancernes omfang bestemmes alene af de bestillinger, som de enkelte Bestillere hos Ordregiver løbende afgiver. Forbruget er således bestemt af det faktiske behov for i Ordregivers afdelinger og institutioner, og Ordregiver er ikke forpligtet til at aftage et vist minimum.Der er i Aftalen krav om en minimumsleveringsgrad, hvorved menes, hvor stor en procentdel af alle bestillinger som den vindende tilbudsgiver skal dække.Kravene er en leveringsgrad på 92 % for Akutvikarer og 95 % for Planlagte vikarer. Såfremt de fastsatte leveringsgrader ikke overholdes, vil der være tale om mislighold der blandt andet vil kunne medføre et krav om betaling af en bod.

description: Am Bildungsstandort Eslohe befindet sich das zentrale Kompetenzzentrum des Dachdeckerhandwerks in Westfalen. Der Standort vereint die schulische Berufsausbildung, die Unterbringung der Auszubildenden, Verpflegungsangebote sowie Maßnahmen der Aus- und Weiterbildung in einem zusammenhängenden Campus. Die bestehende Gebäudeinfrastruktur stammt überwiegend aus den Jahren 1968 und 1985. Die vorhandenen Gebäude entsprechen sowohl hinsichtlich ihrer funktionalen Struktur als auch in Bezug auf die bauliche, energetische und nutzungsspezifische Qualität nicht mehr den heutigen Anforderungen an einen modernen Bildungs- und Internatsstandort. Insbesondere die bestehende Mischnutzung von Unterricht, Verwaltung, Wohnen und Verpflegung innerhalb der vorhandenen Gebäude führt zu organisatorischen Einschränkungen und erschwert eine zeitgemäße Umsetzung des Bildungsauftrags. Auch die Unterbringungssituation im Wohnheimbereich entspricht nicht mehr den aktuellen Anforderungen. Die derzeit überwiegend vorhandenen Mehrbettzimmer mit Gemeinschaftssanitäranlagen bieten nur eingeschränkte Aufenthalts- und Wohnqualität. Darüber hinaus bestehen Defizite bei den Freizeit-, Aufenthalts- und Kommunikationsflächen für die Auszubildenden. Im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurden verschiedene Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten für den Standort untersucht. Auf Grundlage der Ergebnisse hat sich der Auftraggeber für die Realisierung eines Ersatzneubaukonzeptes entschieden. Damit sollen die funktionalen, organisatorischen, pädagogischen und energetischen Anforderungen langfristig erfüllt und gleichzeitig der laufende Schul- und Wohnheimbetrieb während der Realisierung sichergestellt werden.

Für die Erweiterung des Platzangebotes zur Unterbringung von Hort- und Schulplätzen stehen weitere Flächen, wie ein Verkehrsgarten, ein bereits bestehendes Kitagebäude mit ca. 200 Plätzen sowie das Hortgebäude Haus 2 zur Verfügung. Zur Entwicklung des zur Verfügung stehenden Geländes an der Drebkauer Straße zu einem ganzheitlichen Bildungs- und Betreuungsstandort sind zur Sicherstellung der benötigten Betreuungs-kapazitäten ergänzende Hortplätze zu schaffen. Nach aktuellem Stand besteht ein Bedarf von ca. 160 Plätzen. Die planerische Umsetzung der mit dem Nutzer abgestimmten Gebäudekonzepte soll sich auch in der Gestaltung der Freiflächen widerspiegeln. Die sich auf dem zu beplanenden Gelände befindlichen Gebäude sollen freianlagentechnisch gefasst und somit zu einem stimmigen Gesamtbild verschmelzen. Als Ergebnis der planerischen Überlegungen soll eine altersgerechte und vielfältig nutzbare (Bewegung, Spiel, Rückzug, Sport) Außenfläche das Ziel sein. Die genauen Angaben entnehmen Sie bitte der Leistungsbeschreibung.

description: Evakuierungsarbeiten von Pipelines zum Gastransport Abfackeln von Restmengen Inertisieren von Pipelines zum Gastransport Im Rahmen einer nicht abschließenden Rahmenvereinbarung (1) GASCADE Gastransport GmbH und (2) NEL Gastransport GmbH (NGT) sind unabhängige Fernleitungsnetzbetreiber mit Sitz in Kassel, Deutschland. Die Auftraggeber sind Tochtergesellschaften der Wiga Transport Beteiligungs-GmbH & Co. KG, die wiederum zur SEFE Securing Energy for Europe GmbH gehört. GASCADE und NGT transportieren Erdgas und Wasserstoff sicher, zuverlässig und effizient durch ihre Pipelinesysteme. Die Auftraggeber spielen eine wichtige Rolle bei der Förderung einer nachhaltigen Energiezukunft und unterstützen den Aufbau eines Wasserstoff-Netzes in Deutschland und Europa. Die Auftraggeber sind auch an verschiedenen Projekten beteiligt, die zur Verbesserung der Gasinfrastruktur und zur Unterstützung der Energiewende beitragen. Die EU-Methanregulierung verpflichtet die Auftraggeber als Fernleitungsnetzbetreiber alle Maßnahmen möglichst Emissionsfrei durchzuführen. Der Einsatz von mobilen Umpumpverdichtern, Fackel und anschließender Inertisierung bietet den Auftraggebern die Möglichkeit, Arbeiten an den Assets mit möglichst geringen Emissionen durchzuführen. Dieses Leistungsverzeichnis beschreibt die Erbringung von drei Arbeitsschritten: das Evakuieren, Abfackeln und Inertisieren. Das Medium ist Erdgas und Wasserstoff der 5. Gasfamilie nach G260. Die mobilen Einheiten sollen über flexible Schlauchleitungen oder Chiksan Leitungen angeschlossen werden können. Das Verbrauchsgas sowie die evakuierte/abgefackelte Menge soll gemessen und dokumentiert werden. Die Rahmenvereinbarung tritt mit Zuschlagserteilung durch den oder die Auftraggeber in Kraft, wobei sich die Auftraggeber gegenseitig vertreten können. Der Zuschlag zum Abschluss, der nicht abschließenden Rahmenvereinbarung wird, allen Bietern erteilt, die nicht auszuschließen sind, die geforderten Eignungsanforderungen erfüllen, die Rahmenvereinbarung vorbehaltlos akzeptieren und für mindestens ein beantragtes Leis-tungspaket sämtliche Mindestanforderungen erfüllen. Eine Preiswertung findet im Verfahren zum Abschluss der Rahmenvereinbarung nicht statt. Die Vergabestelle schätzt das anstehende Auftragsvolumen über die Laufzeit auf EUR 15.000.000,00. Der Gesamtwert aller Einzelaufträge aus der Rahmenvereinbarung ist daher auf den Höchstwert von EUR 20.000.000,00 netto begrenzt. Nach Erreichen des Höchstwerts dürfen keine weiteren Einzelaufträge auf Grundlage der Rahmenvereinbarung vergeben werden. Die Auftraggeber führen eine gemeinsame fortlaufende Abrufkontrolle. Der Ausführungszeitraum der einzelnen konkreten Beauftragungen wird bei Bedarf mittels Mini-Wettbewerb bekannt gegeben. Die Laufzeit der Rahmenvereinbarung endet, ohne dass es einer Kündigung bedarf, wenn der Höchstwert oder die Höchstmenge der Rahmenvereinbarung durch die Vergabe von Einzelaufträgen erschöpft ist oder nach 8 Jahren, je nachdem, welches Ereignis früher eintritt. Weitere Details siehe Vergabeunterlagen.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MINERAL PROCESSING LEASING OPPORTUNITIES
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is the first phase of a process to leverage non-excess under-utilized Department of the Air Force (DAF) surface land to accelerate economic development in the United States and to enhance mission readiness in connection with presidential directives and policy directing agencies to leverage federal assets to support mineral processing facilities, to include processing of rare earth elements. For purposes of this RFI, mineral processing is strictly limited to surface use activities, including refining, and smelting of minerals, and the production of processed critical minerals and other derivative products. This RFI does not solicit interest in the exploration or extraction of subsurface minerals. While the Department of the Interior/Bureau of Land Management (DOI/BLM) generally controls the leasing and disposition of federally owned subsurface minerals, the DAF maintains authority over whether and under what conditions a party may physically occupy or use the surface of a DAF installation consistent with mission requirements.

title: Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP) Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) Supplemental Request for Information (RFI) � Industry Statements of Capability (SOCs)
description: Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP) Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) Supplemental Request for Information (RFI) � Industry Statements of Capability (SOCs): 1. RIDE Overview (Updated): The Space Systems Command (SSC), System Delta 80 (SYD 80), Small Launch and Targets Division (AMX) manages the Rocket Systems Launch Program (RSLP). Supplemental to the previous RFI posted on 25 April 2025 (https://sam.gov/opp/19f4b8b3647940b48fa14134d23249a9/view#contact), RSLP still plans to execute its suborbital and orbital launch services by employing its new RSLP Innovative Delivery of Effects (RIDE) acquisition strategy. RIDE acquisitions will serve as the next generation of RSLP launch service contracts, succeeding the Orbital Services Program-4 (OSP-4), Small Rocket Program-Orbital (SRP-O), and Sounding Rocket Program-4 (SRP-4) programs. RSLP will continue to provide responsive space, experimental, Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E), and small operational launch vehicles and targets support to the Department of War (DoW) and other Government agencies using commercial services and excess ballistic missile assets. RIDE acquisitions are intended to support a wide variety of customer-driven requirements that may not traditionally fall within the scope of NSSL requirements, from integration and launch of payloads intended for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and beyond, to suborbital vehicle development, and more. Given the variety of launch missions with varying degrees of complexity that RSLP anticipates supporting, the RIDE acquisition strategy may result in one (1) or more contract vehicles [such as an indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract, which is currently being considered]. In response to industry feedback captured by RSLP�s first RFI solicitation, Attachment 1 of this RFI contains updated high-level requirements of the RIDE acquisition strategy. These requirements are still subject to change. 2. Background (Unchanged): RSLP has historically launched one-off launch systems for RDT&E type payloads, from unguided lofted trajectories to cis-lunar orbit. In the past, industry offered limited launch service options capable of meeting the wide range of mission performance required. This led to RSLP managing many first-flight vehicles, or vehicles with first-flight items, to meet our customers� needs. The management of those first-flight vehicles and items shaped the mission assurance practices that RSLP implemented and continues to use today. Our customers, mainly from the RDT&E community with limited budgets, drive mission assurance requirements based on their risk tolerance. A higher level of risk is more often deemed acceptable for the payloads than for the launch vehicles. RSLP recognizes that industry�s capability and capacity have changed greatly over the last 10 years. RSLP is therefore assessing those changes and determining how to best meet the launch service needs of our U.S. Government customers. There is a wide variance in the experience, vehicle heritage, and production and manufacturing processes observed across the commercial launch industry today. This variance offers opportunities to ensure fair competition while providing varying levels of mission assurance across different customer requirement driven missions. 3. RIDE Acquisition Background (Added): RIDE is intended to enable RSLP to provide an encompassing launch service acquisition solution in support of the United States Space Force (USSF), DoW, and other Government customers. In doing so, it is anticipated that RIDE will provide a means to support both Space Transportation Services [as defined in 51 U.S. Code � 50101(4); which are considered inherently commercial in accordance with 51 U.S. Code � 50132] and Space-Related Activity launch services [as defined in 51 U.S. Code � 50101(3); which are�for the purposes of this contemplated acquisition strategy�not assumed to be inherently commercial] required by various programs with various payloads. Space Transportation Services involve the preparation as well as transportation of a launch vehicle and its payloads to, from, or within outer space, or in suborbital trajectory. Space-Related Activity launch services include research and development (R&D), which is more in-depth or complex than a traditional Space Transportation Service. Additionally, Space-Related Activity launch services may require new design, significant modifications, extensive supplemental qualification testing, and/or developmental concept of operations (CONOPs). To support both Space Transportation and Space-Related Activity launches, the Government is contemplating the use of two (2) multiple-award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicles; one (1) for Space Transportation Services and [commercial] Space-Related Activity launch services and one (1) for [non-commercial] Space-Related Activity launch services: Space Transportation Services will be procured as a commercial service, leveraging commercial practices on a fixed-price [e.g., Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), fixed-price incentive, fixed-price with award fee, etc.] basis. Additionally, certain Space-Related Activity services which are determined to be commercial by the cognizant Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) at the time of the contemplated effort shall also be acquired under the commercial IDIQ and will also utilize a fixed-price structure. Due to the developmental/non-commercial nature of many of the anticipated Space-Related Activity services, the Government anticipates issuing hybrid cost-reimbursement [e.g., Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee (CPIF), cost-reimbursement incentive, cost-plus award fee, etc.] and FFP task orders under the non-commercial IDIQ, as appropriate for the specific requirement (again, to be decided by the cognizant PCO at the time of the contemplated effort). Companies should consider whether they possess, or can obtain, the systems and capabilities necessary to perform cost-reimbursement contracts, including an improved accounting system IAW R-DFARS 242.7502 (implemented by 48 CFR 242.7502) and comply with the system criteria prescribed in R-DFARS 252.242-7998 (if applicable) and DFARS 252.242.7999 (Deviation 2026-O0050) (March 2026). A company may compete for entry into the vendor pool of one (1) or both IDIQs, but must follow and satisfy the proposal requirements for each IDIQ if they wish to compete for both. 4. RFI Goals and Objectives (Updated): The goal of this second RFI is to collect Statements of Capability (SOCs) from industry on available solutions, technologies, and capabilities to aid in further defining the RIDE acquisition requirements and future commerciality determinations. These SOCs will help RSLP understand how industry capabilities currently align with the anticipated Government requirements and the mission type(s) to which vendors plan to propose. Please engage with us by providing your company�s SOC(s) to address the attached tentative requirements. 5. Industry Day (Added): RSLP intends to host a forum with industry (i.e., �Industry Day�) on 22 September 2026 through 23 September 2026 (or possibly through 24 September 2026, depending on the number of RSVP�d attendees) to engage in open discussion and dialogue to answer questions interested parties may have regarding the Government�s contemplated RIDE acquisition strategy prior to SOC submittal. The objective of this two (2) to three (3)-day event is to receive industry�s feedback on RSLP�s intent of the RIDE acquisition and to provide industry with additional details about the RIDE acquisition prior to the SOC submittal date. Interested companies will have the option of participating virtually if they choose or may attend in-person on Kirtland AFB, located in Albuquerque, NM. title: Blanket Purchase Agreement-Machine Tools and Equipment
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 and FAR Part 16, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) China Lake, CA facilitates a variety of weapons and energetics research, development, testing and evaluation programs in support of Naval operations. To accelerate cost-effective and rapid response methods, NAWCWD is awarding Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) under Machine tools and Equipment and competing requirements through the Lakehurst BPA Tool to the BPA holders within each commodity. Synopsis/Solicitation N6893626Q5152 is being issued as an invitation to small business concerns that are interested in becoming prospective vendors for the Machine Tools and Equipment found in attachment 1. In accordance with RFO Part 19, the Government�s intent is to establish BPAs with Small Businesses; therefore, this requirement is Set Aside for Small Business. The BPA Calls issued will incorporate clauses that are prescribed by the RFO, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and the Navy and Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS). Please note that a BPA is not a contract. A BPA is a method for filling anticipated repetitive needs for supplies by establishing �charge accounts� with qualified sources of supply. The Government is only obligated to the extent of authorized purchases actually placed under a BPA. All calls must be acknowledged by the selected vendors to be retained on the BPA calling list. This combined synopsis/solicitation will allow for the review of interested companies� qualifications and result in the award of BPAs. The Government does not intend to pay for any information provided under this combined synopsis/solicitation. The Government is not obligated to notify respondents of the results of this combined synopsis/solicitation. Prospective vendors are invited to submit their responses to this combined synopsis/solicitation within the next 60 days, as vendors will be added on a rolling basis throughout the lifetime of the BPA commodities program. Once a contractor is issued a BPA there is no need to submit any response to subsequent combined synopsis/solicitation postings. Contractors are cautioned that their BPA may not be renewed or may be cancelled if the contractor is not actively participating in the program by submitting bids in the Lakehurst BPA Tool or consistently have poor performance. The maximum value of each individual purchase under a BPA may not exceed the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. Payments will be made using Government Purchase Credit (GPC) cards or electronic invoice submission IAW DFARS 252.232-7006 �Wide Area Workflow Instructions (JAN 2023).� Third party payment systems will not be accepted. The Nonmanufacturer rule will apply to all nonmanufacturers in accordance with RFO FAR Part 19.104. A nonmanufacturer means any concern, including a supplier, that provides an end item it did not manufacture, process or produce. The contractor shall supply Machine Equipment and Tools to be delivered Free on Board (FOB) Destination terms to China Lake Applied Manufactured Technology Division (AMTD) located onboard NAWCWD China Lake, CA. It will be specified in the BPA Call. Attachment 1 includes a list of Machine and Tools with NAICS Codes but is not limited to just this list. Note: further requirements may be specified for each separate BPA Call. Delivery times will be specified at the BPA Call level. Interested parties shall provide their Cage Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEID) Numbers for verification of inclusion in the System for Award Management (SAM) along with a capabilities statement. The capabilities statement should include what the contractor�s primary business practice/trade is, and whether the contractor is a manufacturer or a supplier/distributor. Responsibility determinations will also precede issuance of a BPA call and will be conducted in accordance with RFO FAR Part 9.1

title: Satellite Phones and Service Plan
description: This Sources Sought is part of the U.S. Government's market research efforts to identify capable vendors for supplying satellite phones and associated prepaid global service plans listed in the attached Statement of Work (SOW). The information gathered will help inform future procurement strategies and requirements. This Sources Sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. Respondents are encouraged to review the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW). Note: The attached SOW currently specifies delivery to the INL Mexico warehouse (Trafimar, Naucalpan) with the contractor responsible for importation. The Government is evaluating an alternative delivery model to Brownsville, TX, with the Government handling importation into Mexico. Respondents should address both scenarios in Question 1 below. Responding to this Sources Sought Responses are limited to no more than 10 pages in length using 14 point Font Size. The Government prefers that your firm submit its response in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat, or a combination of both and the document must be searchable. Please identify the following about your company: Name of Company, Unique Entity ID (UEI), and CAGE Code Point of contact name, phone number, and email address Business Type: Small Business Small Disadvantaged Business 8(a) � certified Small Disadvantaged Business HUBZone Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) Other than small business Response should provide a brief overview of your company. Table A of the attached Statement of Work includes the technical specifications for the equipment covered by this requirement. Respondents should address the following questions in their responses: Delivery Location � Feasibility Comparison: Please indicate which delivery scenario is more feasible for your company, and explain why: (a) Delivery to Brownsville, TX, with the U.S. Government (INL Logistics) handling importation into Mexico and the vendor providing all the required exportation licenses/permits; or (b) Delivery to the INL Mexico warehouse (Trafimar, Naucalpan, Estado de M�xico), with your company responsible for importation, customs clearance, and acting as importer of record. Please address estimated cost, lead time, and any logistical risks associated with each option. Can your company provide a prepaid global satellite service plan for each phone, good for 720 days with a minimum of 6,000 minutes, that is serviceable in Mexico? Please describe plan activation timing and whether SIM cards would be pre-activated prior to delivery. Besides the SIM cards and the prepaid global satellite service plan, is there any other technical requirement needed for the phones to be operational in Mexico? Will technical support for the service plan be available in Mexico, in Spanish, to assist end users with service issues or troubleshooting? Can your company offer a 12-month warranty that is valid and serviceable in Mexico, without requiring the equipment to be exported out of Mexico for repair or replacement? Does your company have local representation or a partner in Mexico capable of fulfilling warranty claims? Do you have an existing office, warehouse, or local partner in Mexico to support warranty and service plan obligations? If so, please describe the relationship and services provided. Can your company perform operational capability testing of all satellite phones, SIM cards, and service plans? Please explain how. Importation Experience (if Scenario (b) applies): If your company would be responsible for importing equipment into Mexico, does it have experience shipping equipment into Mexico? Is your company familiar with Mexican customs and import regulations? Please provide specific examples of past compliance. What risks, if any, do you foresee under either delivery scenario � including meeting delivery timelines, activating/maintaining the prepaid plan in Mexico, or supporting the in-country warranty? How would your company mitigate them? Besides the delivery risks, does your company identify any areas in the SOW that represent excessive risks or other concerns for the implementation of this project? If so, please provide detailed information and suggested mitigation. Response Submission Deadline Please provide your responses to this Request for Information (RFI) by October 9, 2026. Sources Sought Submissions will be accepted as email attachments only. All responses must be sent to Alexander Bring (BringAG@state.gov), with 19AQMM26NSATPHONE - Satellite Phones for Vetted Units in the subject Line.
